title: Hermes-agent as personal AI infrastructure
summary: A node for automation that becomes part of the working environment rather than a novelty demo.
detail:
Released by Nous Research in 2026, Hermes doesn’t just answer questions — it learns, remembers, and evolves with you. Every successful task becomes a reusable skill stored as clean Markdown. 

It reflects on what worked, refines its approach, and builds a living knowledge base tailored exactly to your life and work. The longer you use it, the more powerful it becomes.This is persistence done right. Hermes runs 24/7 on your own machine or cheap VPS. 

All your data stays private in a local database — no cloud company owns your thoughts. Start a research task on your laptop, continue it from your phone via Telegram, and get updates on WhatsApp. It feels like texting a collaborator who never sleeps. Model-agnostic by design, it lets you plug in any brain you want: local Ollama, Grok, Claude, GPTx or whatever’s strongest next week. 

Forty-plus tools give it real reach — web browsing, image generation, code execution, home automation, scheduling, and computer use.

title: Bill Evans - the jazz pianist who took giant steps
summary: Marked by tragedy, gentle genius met dense jazz harmony and became an inspiration to generations of jazz pianists.
detail: Evans’s thoughtful, lyrical, and harmonically sophisticated approach was a perfect foil for Miles Davis’ sparse, cool trumpet style. Their brief time together helped push jazz toward modal improvisation and greater freedom — a shift that defined Kind of Blue, still one of the best-selling and most influential jazz albums ever.
